name: Duotone
basis: a gradient map: tone mixed between two colours (how)
note: Named after two-ink offset duotones, but models neither the plates nor ink overprint.

lumenary.blurb: Every tone mapped onto a blend between two colours: darks one, lights the other.

facts.era: 20th century, popular in digital branding since the 2010s
facts.bestOn: Pictures with strong light and shade

why: Duotone throws away colour and keeps tone, then pours the tone into two inks. Every pixel is brightness only, mixed between a shadow colour and a highlight colour. That constraint is why duotone ties a set of mixed photographs together so well: whatever the original colours, they all end up in the same pair.
how: Turn each pixel into a single brightness value.
Bend it with a power curve so the midpoint slider decides which brightness lands halfway between the two colours.
Mix between the shadow and highlight colours by that value.
Add a little film grain to prevent banding in smooth gradients.
history: In printing a duotone uses two inks, often black and a spot colour, to give a photograph a richer tonal range than black alone. In the 2010s brands such as Spotify popularised bold digital duotones for imagery, and the technique became a staple of social and music graphics.
uses: Brand imagery with a consistent look
Poster series with a shared palette
terms: A single ink printed by itself rather than mixed from others.
The brightness that falls exactly halfway between the two colours.
Visible steps in a smooth gradient.
paragraphs: Duotone throws away colour and keeps tone. Each pixel’s brightness is first bent by a power curve so that the “midpoint” slider decides which brightness lands exactly halfway between the two colours, then given more or less contrast, and finally used as the mix between your shadow colour and your highlight colour. Black becomes the first, white the second, and everything else is a straight blend of the two.

Because only one number per pixel survives, the effect depends entirely on the tonal map of the picture, which is why a good duotone starts from a picture with strong light and shade. A little film grain is added at the end to stop the smooth gradients from banding.

equations.note: Tone t: L is brightness, m the midpoint slider (0.2 to 0.8; L = m maps to ½) and c the contrast slider.
A is the shadow colour and B the highlight colour, mixed per channel.

presets.text: Ocean tones are cool and calm.
Acid colours with high contrast look like a club flyer.
Move the midpoint toward the shadows to brighten the picture.
